Title: Benchmarking GraphRAG - how do you measure benefit?
Speaker: Joe Eaton & Bradley Rees
Description:
GraphRAG is currently a hot topic with its promise of improving the quality of LLM generated answers by augmenting the query with multi-hop facts extracted from a Knowledge Graph (KG). But how is the GraphRAG system being tested to validate that it is truly providing a benefit?
Large (and Small) Language Models (LLMs) have shown that they can understand languages and provide Question and Answering chatbot solutions. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves upon LLM by adding local/private knowledge. However, even with RAG, LLM systems still can either fail to answer multi-step reasoning questions or just hallucinate (make up) the answer. The solution is to extend RAG with graph-based facts and create a GraphRAG system.
A GraphRAG solution can be viewed as being comprised of three parts: (1) Ingest, the extraction of facts from documents; (2) the Knowledge Graph, where facts are saved, and (3) retrieval, the extraction of data from the KG for question answering. Each of those parts influences how well GraphRAG will work. Therefore, each component needs to be benchmarked for both accuracy and speed. Furthermore, there is the issue of how to evaluate the results generated by the GraphRAG solution. A common approach is to use another LLM to evaluate the answer, but there is no guarantee that the evaluation LLM will know the correct answer.
This talk will present an overview of GraphRAG and dive into the various components. The talk will then discuss ways to benchmark the overall GraphRAG solution, explore in what cases does GraphRAG perform better than Vector-only RAG and even pure LLM, and how to benchmark the subcomponents. The talk will also present some of the emerging benchmarking proposals.

Title: Knowledge Infrastructures and the Ontology Pipeline for AI Systems
Speaker: Jessica Talisman
Description:
How do we build reliable, accurate AI agents and systems that scale across AI workloads? How can we engineer high quality data pipelines delivering context-rich knowledge ecosystems for both humans and machines?
The Ontology Pipeline is a knowledge graph-based framework for designing and constructing semantic knowledge infrastructures powering AI. Its iterative logical steps—from controlled vocabularies, taxonomies, and metadata schemas to thesauri, ontologies, and knowledge graphs—harmonize data from diverse sources into structured, AI-ready assets.
Discover how ontologies resolve semantic heterogeneity, boost interoperability, accelerate advanced AI analytics, and drive knowledge discovery. Explore real world use cases and best practices for transforming unstructured and syntactic data into semantically rich, actionable assets underpinning AI workloads.

Title: Intelligent Data for Life Sciences - Beyond the Hype, how Tailored Graph-AI Solutions Change the Game
Speaker: Cedric Berger
Description:
The problem being addressed: Transforming the drug development industry from siloed, manual, document-centric activities to an end-to-end, automated, data-centric process.
As the internet increasingly presents more challenges than solutions, technology vendors continue to make bold promises about AI. However, only a select few—whether individuals or organizations—will truly benefit from it. This disparity hinges on the culture, people, mindsets, and skills that will enable the understanding, adoption, implementation, and oversight of digital solutions.
By exploring various use cases from the Life Sciences sector, I will show how organizations can effectively implement graph+AI solutions, assess and monitor their value, and regain control over their data mess (not mesh).
Over the past decade, I have implemented knowledge graph and AI solutions, including graph RAG since 2022, to address specific business use cases in the Life Science, whether successfully or unsuccessfully.
Track record of improving processes and business practices using data-centricity and AI in biomedical research, drug development and manufacturing domains (https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.02082).
Target audience
Both business and technical
Intermediate technical
Biomedical, life science industry
What will the people who attend your talk get from it

Title: What Your AI is Allowed to Know: Identity and Graphs in AI Security
Speaker: Alexandre Babeanu
Description:
AI is the Wild West of the new digital frontier. Organizations are rapidly deploying LLM-powered agents and knowledge-based systems with access to vast, contextualized data and knowledge graphs—often without regard for confidentiality, data protection, or trade secrets. These systems are designed to please the prompter—human or machine—and will retrieve whatever knowledge best serves the prompt, regardless of who’s asking.
But not all knowledge should be available to everyone. So how should we enforce proper access control in this new AI-powered world, and protect our secrets? Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) worked fine last century, but it is completely out of its depth when tackling the complexities inherent to fine-grained access control to knowledge. It is time to use a new paradigm for a new era!
In this session, we explore Knowledge-Based Access Control (KBAC)—a dynamic, context-aware approach to restricting access to knowledge using the graph itself. You’ll learn how KBAC goes beyond static rules to:
Evaluate access permissions in real-time based on graph contextUnderstand who should or shouldn’t have access—and whyPredict future access needsAssess user or agent intent dynamically
This talk weaves together identity, authorization, and knowledge graphs, topics that are crucial for securing AI applications in the enterprise.

Title: How to implement Ontology Based Data Management – Moving from application-centric to data-centric
Speaker: Ben Gardner
Description:
In most organisations, the data strategy is focused on generating data for its primary use. This approach priorities delivery of the application, process or service over reuse or repurposing of data. The consequence of this application-centric approach is fragmentation and siloing of data.
This creates significant difficult when combing data across applications or connecting processes that run across functions. If an organisation wants to realise the value from their data, they must unlock the significant value in their data to enable orthogonal use cases i.e. data science, process automation and the transformative opportunities presented by artificial intelligence. This means becoming data-centric and pivoting to make data reuse a first-class citizen.
In AstraZeneca we are solving this problem by taking the hard-won lessons learnt from building large scale knowledge graphs and applying these to delivering an Ontology Based Data Management (OBDM) for the organisation. This means:
Starting with meaning and identifying the things that matter (a reference model)Deciding how to categorise these things and building controlled vocabularies (taxonomies)Making the data interoperable and reusable (applying FAIR Principles)At the heart of this is application of semantic technologies and W3C standards but the key to adoption has been to hide this away and enable the data scientists and engineers to realise the benefits in the tools/technology stacks they are already using.
As a result for the first time, we are driving standardisation into our data. This is delivering new insights from clinical data, efficiencies in cross functional processes, enabling data scientist to focus on science and underpinning agentic AI.
In this masterclass we will describe the OBDM approach from a people, process, technology and content perspective. Key components of this approach will be explored using real life examples. At the end you will understand the pivot we have made from putting data into the graph to putting the graph into the data.

Title: Graphs in the Real World: Modelling for Complex Enterprises
Speaker: Xanthos Angelides & Mark Manley
Description:
Knowledge graphs power the systems we use every day, from search engines to recommendation platforms. Behind these systems lies a model: a connected view of data drawn from different sources, enriched with rules that give meaning to the relationships. This modelling process is what enables knowledge graphs to support complex use cases, from answering questions to generating recommendations.
In this masterclass, we will explore how dataflows provide a practical way to build such models. A dataflow offers a visual and repeatable approach for transforming structured data into RDF, applying business rules and linking domains into a unified graph. By defining how different pieces of data connect, dataflows turn raw inputs into a meaningful, queryable model.
Using files that represent domains of a telecom network, we will build a knowledge graph step by step. Participants will see how to load structured data, apply rules to model relationships across domains, and query the graph to generate useful visualizations of the network.
Designed for data scientists and engineers of all levels, this session introduces the high-level concepts of modelling with knowledge graphs while providing hands-on skills for creating them. You will leave with an understanding of how dataflows bridge raw data and connected models - the foundation of the intelligent systems we rely on every day.

Title: Rules for speed, simplicity, and data-centricity
Speaker: Ivo Velitchkov
Description:
Public procurement in the European Economic Area is a vast and complex system: 250,000 public agencies spend around 2.5 trillion EUR each year (15% of GDP) on services, works, and supplies.
Yet the data behind this enormous market remains fragmented, stuck in silos, and split across incompatible formats, schemas, and local legal practices. Even where EU regulations apply, the process is document-centric and difficult to analyse. The result is a lack of interoperability that obstructs policymaking, transparency, accountability, and equal access to opportunities.
This is the problem the Public Procurement Data Space (PPDS) seeks to address.
PPDS is the first and currently the only public procurement semantic data space in the world and one of the largest knowledge graph projects in the public sector.
Unlike other data spaces, which typically stop at metadata and connectors, PPDS builds a full knowledge graph of procurement data. Complying with the FAIR principles is already demanding, but committing also to data-centric principles makes the task even more challenging.
This talk will focus on how PPDS addresses these challenges with rules covering query performance, analytics, graph generation, and data governance. While the approach uses different kinds of rules, the main emphasis will be on inference rules, all implemented in SHACL.
The approach is not procurement-specific: the way rules are defined and governed can be applied in other sectors. The project has also developed an openly available rule governance methodology.
Target audience: technical and business participants
Level: intermediate (no procurement knowledge required; some familiarity with RDF helpful)
Takeaways:
Lessons from one of the largest knowledge graph implementations in Europe
Practical methods for solving knowledge graph challenges with rules, especially SHACL rules
Access to a reusable methodology for rule governance

Title: Combine Knowledge Graphs and LLMs to speed up criminal network analysis: A hands-on tour
Speaker: Alessandro Negro
Description:
Organisations across domains collect vast relational data but struggle to extract meaningful patterns and generate professional intelligence reports from complex networks. Traditional approaches require weeks of manual analysis, miss critical relationships, and produce inconsistent results. The technical challenge lies in combining graph analytics with AI systems that provide reliable, explainable outputs suitable for high-stakes decision-making.
This masterclass addresses the implementation gap: while organisations recognise the potential of Knowledge Graphs + LLMs, they lack practical guidance for building reliable systems that handle real-world data complexity and produce professional-quality analysis.
Why This Matters: Attendees will learn a complete technical methodology that applies beyond criminal networks to fraud detection, supply chain analysis, cybersecurity, and any domain requiring relationship analysis at scale. The techniques covered—graph data science, agentic AI coordination, systematic prompt engineering, and quality evaluation—represent reusable patterns for building explainable AI systems in critical applications.
Technical Approach and Hands-On Learning
Phase 1: Graph-Powered Network Analysis
Transform raw relational data into meaningful co-occurrence networks using association strength calculationsApply community detection (Louvain) and centrality measures (PageRank, Betweenness) with practical implementation examplesExtract structured intelligence from graph analysis for AI processingPhase 2: Agentic AI Implementation
Build LangGraph workflows with parallel agent coordinationImplement systematic prompt engineering techniques with measurable quality improvementsDesign LLMs-as-judge evaluation systems with bias mitigation protocolsGenerate professional HTML reports through coordinated AI agentsDemonstrated Impact: Participants will implement a complete pipeline that processes complex relational data and generates comprehensive analysis reports. The methodology reduces analysis time from weeks to hours while discovering patterns invisible through manual approaches, with reliability suitable for operational deployment.
Target Audience
Level: Intermediate to Advanced TechnicalBackground: Experience with graph databases, familiarity with Python, basic understanding of LLMs and network analysis conceptsRole: Data scientists, AI engineers, technical architects, analysts working with complex relational dataWhat Attendees Will Learn:
Technical Implementation Skills:

Title: Collaborative Information Exchange Environments using NIEMOpen with Ontologies and Knowledge Graphs
Speaker: Bradley Bolliger
Description:
Modernizing legacy information systems can be an arcane process with aging infrastructure, legacy data challenges, and limited funding relative to core operational concerns. Facilitating the connectedness of critical data infrastructure and meeting the collaborative analytical needs of our modern world require semantically-aligned information exchange across distributed systems.
Achieve a common vocabulary for modeling complex systems using knowledge graphs as a design aid to analyze a problem space, align information flows to business need, and design extensible entity-centric data models.
These techniques in conjunction serve as a foundation for modelling behaviour in information systems and how to apply ontologies and knowledge graphs which align directly to machine-readable data.

Title: Rumble in the Jungle: SPARQL vs SQL vs Cypher
Speaker: Nikolaos Karalis
Description:
Modern companies face an ever-growing volume of data, and deciding how to manage it—relational databases, NoSQL, or graphs—can be challenging. Knowledge graphs provide a flexible, scalable, and semantically rich solution that enables pay-as-you-go data strategies without sacrificing speed or transparency.
Understanding and leveraging knowledge graphs is increasingly critical for building intelligent, data-driven applications. Attendees will gain practical skills that can improve data management, enhance decision-making, and unlock the potential of semantic technologies in real-world scenarios.
This hands-on masterclass introduces the Resource Description Framework (RDF) and SPARQL, demonstrating how to create, query, and explore knowledge graphs. Using Tentris as a practical storage solution, participants will see how RDF and SPARQL compare to relational (SQL) and property graph (Cypher) approaches and learn how to combine these technologies with large language models (LLMs) for advanced applications.
Attendees will leave with the ability to design and query semantic data models, understand the advantages of RDF and SPARQL over traditional database models, and apply these techniques to build intelligent, data-driven applications.
Target Audience:
Business / Technical: Data Scientists, Data Engineers, Data Analysts, Machine Learning Engineers, Knowledge Graph Enthusiasts, CXOsLevel: Beginner to IntermediateRequired Background: Basic knowledge of the command line; familiarity with SQL or Cypher is a plus but not required; no prior knowledge of RDF or SPARQL necessaryTakeaways for Attendees:
Hands-on experience creating and querying RDF knowledge graphsUnderstanding SPARQL’s advantages over SQL and CypherSkills to leverage semantic technologies for intelligent applicationsPractical insight into combining RDF/SPARQL with LLMsFormat:
Short lecture followed by live demos and exercisesParticipants can follow along using their command line interface

Title: Grounding LLMs on Solid Knowledge: Assessing and Improving Knowledge Graph Quality in GraphRAG Applications
Speaker: Panos Alexopoulos
Description:
Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by grounding their outputs in structured knowledge graphs, leading to more accurate, domain-relevant, and explainable responses.
However, many of the graphs used in such pipelines are either auto-generated or loosely constructed, often lacking the semantic precision, structure, and consistency needed for dependable grounding. This can result in weak retrieval, vague or misleading answers, and hallucinations that are hard to detect or debug.
This hands-on masterclass presents a practical framework for evaluating and improving the quality of knowledge graphs in GraphRAG systems. Participants will examine common failure modes, review real-world case studies, and apply a reusable checklist to determine whether a graph is truly “AI-ready.”
The session will equip attendees with concrete methods to identify modeling flaws, data gaps, and inconsistencies, along with strategies to enhance semantic accuracy and retrieval performance in their GraphRAG implementations.
Target Audience
Knowledge graph practitioners, data architects, modelers, and AI/ML professionals seeking to integrate semantic data into generative AI workflows.
Goals
By the end of the masterclass, participants will be able to:
Understand how GraphRAG worksLearn metrics and tools to evaluate GraphRAG pipelinesIdentify common knowledge graph issues affecting GraphRAG performanceApply practical quality assessment techniques

Title: Fixed Entity Architecture and Cypherouting: GraphRAG made uncomplicated and nearly LLM-free
Speaker: Irina Adamchic
Description:
We often hear that GraphRAG is too expensive, too complicated, and requires highly trained ontologists, making it unappealing for most organizations. But what if we could simplify things and drastically improve our RAG applications using graphs, without such effort?
Fixed Entity Architecture offers a solution by building graphs based on a limited and usually predefined business domain ontology. A layered lexical graph, constructed without the help of LLMs and with a limited number of logically separated layers, can be a viable alternative to the well-known Microsoft GraphRAG.
Cypherouting is a method of querying this graph by leveraging its fixed structure, thereby avoiding the error-prone LLM-based text-to-cypher methods. In this presentation, I will introduce both methodologies and provide examples of their implementations.

Title: Climbing the Knowledge Pyramid: How AstraZeneca's Operations Knowledge Fabric Transforms Pharma Operations Through Connected Data
Speaker: Maria Sorokina
Description:
Enterprise AI initiatives are failing at scale—only 4% of companies create substantial AI value despite massive investments. The core issue is context starvation: while GenAI excels at reasoning, it lacks the nuanced enterprise knowledge and semantic understanding needed to make accurate, trustworthy decisions in complex operational environments. Traditional data architectures treat knowledge graphs as glorified databases, leading to semantic drift, brittle integrations, and AI systems that hallucinate confidently but incorrectly.
As organizations race toward autonomous operations and agentic AI, the ability to encode, access, and leverage enterprise context becomes the defining competitive advantage. Without semantic foundations, AI agents remain general-purpose assistants rather than specialized domain experts. The pharmaceutical industry faces unique challenges with regulatory compliance, complex supply chains, and life-critical decisions—making semantic precision not just valuable, but essential for patient safety and operational excellence.
AstraZeneca's Operations Knowledge Fabric represents a fundamental architectural shift from data lakes to knowledge fabrics. We've implemented a distributed semantic architecture using:
Semantic-first data products with RDF output ports that expose ontology-conformant interfacesLayered ontology model from foundational concepts to application-specific vocabulariesLiving ontologies that serve as executable interfaces, not static documentationGraph-native infrastructure built on neo4j and Cognite, integrated with Snowflake data foundationsAI-enabled tooling through our Operations Semantic Platform for rapid ontology developmentRather than centralizing knowledge in databases, we embed semantics directly into data products and knowledge graphs, creating an interconnected web of meaning across manufacturing, supply chain, and drug development operations.
Impact and Results
Accelerated AI deployment: Manufacturing insight agents now provide precise root-cause analysis by traversing semantic relationshipsReduced development time: From 4-6 months for traditional data products to 4-6 days for semantic-enabled solutionsEnhanced decision quality: AI systems understand domain context, regulatory constraints, and operational nuancesFuture-ready architecture: Positioned for autonomous operations and collaborative AI agents through the AZ 2030 bold ambition

Title: From Pipelines to Knowledge: What Data Engineers & Governance Professionals Must Know About Knowledge Graphs
Speaker: Juan Sequeda
Description:
Generative AI has pushed organizations to rethink how they manage and connect their data. But while technology moves fast, the fundamentals remain: if you don’t understand what your data means, your systems will never be truly AI-ready.
This talk is for data engineers and data governance practitioners who want to understand where knowledge graphs fit, and why they matter now more than ever. We’ll unpack the practical intersection between semantics, data governance, and data engineering, showing how knowledge graphs can bridge business context and technical pipelines.
Through a pay-as-you-go methodology, we’ll explore how to capture business meaning, implement it in a machine-readable way, and build reusable, trusted systems that power both analytics and AI. Along the way, we’ll share real-world lessons on moving from pipelines to purpose, creating AI-ready knowledge architectures without boiling the ocean.
Whether you’re transforming data, defining metrics, or enabling AI, you’ll walk away with actionable techniques to make knowledge-first governance and engineering real.
Organizations need their data to be AI-ready. They are already investing heavily in data engineering and governance but still struggle to connect technical pipelines to business meaning. The audience doing that work would benefit from knowledge graphs.
This talk is primarly aimed for 1) data governance/engineer professionals to learn how knowledge graphs can help their work and 2) for knowledge graph professionals to translate how they can help data governance and engineering. This is a gap and my talk will bridge it.
Why It’s Important:
For attendees: Learn how to bridge data engineering, governance, and semantics to enable trusted, AI-ready systems.For data engineers: how to connect business context to the technical data in order to provide semantics from the beginningFor data governance: how represent business context and policies, while not boiling the ocean.For the world: GenAI without meaning leads to hallucinations, inefficiencies, and broken trust. Knowledge graphs solve this by embedding context where it matters most. We need to reach to the people who are already doing this work and give them access to the resources.
How We Address It:
Introduce a pay-as-you-go methodology for knowledge capture, implementation, and validationShow how knowledge graphs integrate technical, mapping and business metadata.Provide real-world examples of applying semantics to data products, metrics, and AI pipelines
Impact:
Exposing Data Governance and Data Engineering professionals to knowledge graphs so they can bring it back to their day to day work.Align business and technical teams around shared meaningReduce duplicated work by making knowledge explicit and reusableEnable trustworthy, explainable AI and scalable governance
Target Audience:
Technical: Primarily focused on data governance and data engineering professionals. Secondary audience are Knowledge Graph professionals who can translate this message to their data governance and engineering colleaguesLevel: Beginner → Intermediate (assumes knowledge of data engineering or governance, but not knowledge graphs)Required Background: Familiarity with data pipelines, metrics, or governance concepts
What Attendees Will Get:
A practical framework for introducing semantics and knowledge graphs into data engineeringA roadmap for applying minimum valuable governance without bureaucracyTechniques for designing AI-ready data systems that scaleThe language and mental models to communicate value across technical and business stakeholders

Title: Combining Data from Structured and Unstructured Sources to create High-Quality Knowledge Graphs
Speaker: Paco Nathan & Prashanth Rao
Description:
An important obstacle for adopting knowledge graph technology in enterprise is that so much enterprise-level data is originally stored in unstructured formats, or in some structured format such as tables – though not as graph data. Therefore, an inevitable first step in adopting graph technologies is to convert these data sources into high-quality knowledge graphs.
This tutorial walks through the different steps of this process and covers a suite of tools and technologies one can use to construct knowledge graphs, run interactive visualizations, and leverage agentic workflows for use cases which need high-quality knowledge graphs.
In this tutorial we will:
Use entity resolution from Senzing to merge OpenSanctions, Open Ownership, and GLEIF datasets.
Load the structured data as Polars dataframes to construct a knowledge graph in KùzuDB.
Annotate the graph for semantic modeling using the FollowTheMoney vocabulary to represent anti-corruption investigations and the BODS vocabulary to represent beneficial ownership.
Add synthetic data for wire transfer transactions among the fraud rings within the graph, to simulate the tradecraft of money laundering.
Develop agentic workflows in BAML to extract entities and relations from news articles about the entities named in the graph.
Leverage graph algorithms in NetworkX: Louvain partitioning to identify subgraphs as potential fraud rings within graph, and betweenness centrality to rank individuals of interest within each subgraphs.
Visualize the subgraphs using yWorks yFile, emphasizing the links to known risks.
Overall, we'll leverage insights from the steps above to identify patterns of fraud tradecraft within the graph, as a fraud analyst at a bank would do.
This pattern of integrating structured and unstructured data sources into a high-quality knowledge graph is an incredibly common need in the real world. Downstream, there may be many kinds of use cases, e.g., graph analytics, dashboards, GraphRAG, question/answer chat bots, agents, and so on.
Key Topics:
open data sources
recognizing patterns of fraud tradecraft
Entity Resolution (ER)
KùzuDB
BODS for representing beneficial ownership
FollowTheMoney for representing anti-corruption investigations
BAML for agentic workflows, extracting from unstructured data sources
NetworkX graph algorithms
yWorks yFiles interactive visualizations
Target Audience:
Data Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers
Data Engineers
Financial Fraud Analysts
Managers of the above
Goals:
Get hands-on experience with tools in Python using high-quality knowledge graphs with graph algorithms and interactive visualization, plus using agentic workflows to augment the graph.
Session Outline:
Open data sources used for anti-fraud investigations
Entity Resolution (ER) to merge different datasets into graph elements
Populating a graph in KùzuDB from Polars dataframes
BODS vocabulary for representing beneficial ownership
FollowTheMoney vocabulary for representing anti-corruption investigations
BAML agentic workflows to extract graph elements from unstructured text
NetworkX graph algorithms to highlight important graph elements
yWorks yFiles for interactive visualizations of subgraphs
Format:
The tutorial will demo on a live example the evaluation of a knowledge graph as it is transformed across steps using several open-source and commercial technologies, such as Senzing, Kùzu (an embedded graph database), BAML, and other supporting libraries.
Be sure to have both Python 3.11 or later installed on your laptop, plus Docker running, and please download the following container images prior to class:
docker pull senzing/demo-senzing
We will start the class with brief lectures introducing the topics, then move into hands-on coding.

Title: Understand relationships in your data with Knowledge Graphs
Speaker: Martin O'Hanlon
Description:
Graph databases give the same importance to relationships as they do to data. Knowledge graphs allow you to uncover insights in your data and efficiently explore the relationships in your data.
In this hands-on workshop you will learn how graph databases can help you find and understand relationships in your data
You will:
- Learn about graph theory, the elements of a graph database, and when a graph database is a good choice for your use case.
- Explore a graph database, learn the basics of the query language Cypher, and use Cypher to read and write data.
- Import your data into a graph database.

Target AudienceData ScientistsData AnalystsSoftware developersManagers of the above
GoalsGet hands-on experience using Neo4j graph database to understand relationships, query and create data.

You will be using Neo4j and the GraphAcademy platform to explore a graph database.
The masterclass will start with an overview of graph and graph database fundamentals and concepts.
You will write queries to find, filter, aggregate and analyse data.
You will import data into an empty database, creating your own data model, and explore how you can import your own data into a graph.
LevelBeginner

Attendees should bring their own laptop, which they will need to access the online workshop material, and, supplied, database. There is no software to pre-install, learners will only need access to a web browser.

Title: Hands On Building Intelligent Memory: Graph Databases for AI Agent Context and Retrieval
Speaker: William Lyon
Description:
As AI agents become increasingly sophisticated, their ability to maintain coherent, retrievable memory across conversations has become the defining factor between basic chatbots and truly intelligent assistants. The challenge isn't just storing information—it's about creating dynamic, interconnected memory systems that help agents understand context, discover relevant connections, and provide personalized responses.
The goal of this masterclass is to take participants from traditional vector-based RAG systems to building production-ready graph-powered memory architectures for AI agents. We will start with conversational data and demonstrate how to extract meaningful entities and relationships, then progressively build a complete graph memory system that evolves with each agent interaction.
Using practical examples with the Vercel AI SDK, participants will implement entity extraction pipelines, design graph schemas for conversational memory, and integrate both Neo4j and Dgraph as complementary solutions. We'll explore direct framework integration patterns versus tool-based approaches through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), giving participants hands-on experience with both architectural strategies.
Once participants are comfortable with basic graph operations and memory retrieval, we will advance into GraphRAG implementations, dynamic context window optimization, and real-time memory evolution techniques. We'll examine how to balance memory persistence with retrieval speed, implement conversation summarization strategies, and handle memory conflicts across multiple conversation threads.
This masterclass is targeted towards AI engineers, backend developers, and technical leads working on conversational AI systems. Participants will learn how to architect intelligent memory systems that transform static AI agents into context-aware, personalized assistants capable of maintaining long-term conversational relationships.
The end result will be that participants can architect and implement graph-powered memory systems from scratch, integrate them seamlessly with modern AI frameworks, and deploy production-ready solutions that significantly enhance agent intelligence and user experience.

Graph modeling principles for conversational AI memory systemsEntity extraction and relationship mapping from conversational dataComparative analysis of Neo4j vs Dgraph for AI agent architecturesDirect integration patterns with Vercel AI SDK and other modern frameworksModel Context Protocol (MCP) implementation for tool-based graph accessGraphRAG implementation strategies and optimization techniquesDynamic memory evolution and conversation summarizationProduction deployment patterns and performance optimization

Build production-ready graph-powered memory systems for AI agents that maintain context across conversations, discover relevant connections, and enable personalized, intelligent responses through hands-on implementation and architectural design.

Format

The session begins with architectural concepts but quickly transitions to practical coding exercises. We'll progress from basic entity extraction to full GraphRAG implementations through guidedcoding sessions.

Participants will build working AI agent memory systems that they can immediately deploy and extend. The workshop includes real conversational datasets for testing and validation, plus debugging sessions to troubleshoot common integration challenges.

Intermediate - Advanced

Title: Creation, Population and Enrichment of Knowledge Graphs with the Help of AI
Speaker: Gulay Canbaloglu
Description:
Organizations involved in the management of physical assets have to deal with vast collections of documents filled with design requirements, recommendations, and best practices. While these documents contain critical qualitative information, they often suffer from fragmented information retrieval, poor version control, limited ownership and insufficient sharing across the value chain.
To overcome this, knowledge graphs facilitate decomposition of each requirement or recommendation into atomic, uniquely identified items, enriched with metadata, interlinked, and related to an ontology. The requirements resulting in enriched text (Bazuin et al., 2023) enable precise retrieval, traceability and collaborative reuse. However, information contained by existing documents must be available as a knowledge graph first.
The challenge of transforming unstructured textual documents into high-quality linked data lies both in the efficient extraction & classification of information, and in the enrichment of the extracted information with metadata. By combining different models, we are able to extract requirements, classify them, and add other relevant metadata.
This presentation showcases a validated implementation based on a language model (based on BERT), which is currently in use in the AECO (Architecture, Engineering and Construction) industry.
The pipeline identifies and classifies requirements from unstructured documents, maps them to semantic models, enriches the data with the help of AI and after validation by domain experts, the resulting datasets are published to a Linked Data platform.
This model already supports the transformation from unstructured documents into structured data, but we will show our current efforts aiming to further automate the enrichment and refinement of these requirements:
Refining requirements to ensure SMARTness (Specific, Measurable, Acchievable, Relevant, Time-bound). This reduces risks during the construction process itself.Linking content to domain-specific ontologies, subjects, or keywords, to enable easier querying.Connecting requirements to solutions, proposals, and lessons learned from other projects.The audience will learn how to combine AI models for creating and enriching knowledge graphs. We will see the application of this pipeline in the AECO industry. Additionally, attendees will get insight in our lessons learned when using AI. We will show how to select the most relevant model, how to keep the human-in-the-loop, and how to scope your approach.
A basic understanding of Linked Data and AI will be helpful for the audience, but not necessary to follow the presentation. We hope to inspire the audience in setting up their own ideas into practice.

Title: The Ultimate Guide to Semantic Reasoning & Knowledge-Based AI: How to enrich your data for practical applications including use with RAG & LLMs
Speaker: Tom Vout
Description:
Semantic reasoning is fast becoming a must-have for anyone running a knowledge graph application as a route to better data, faster queries, and ultimately greater insights.
Knowledge-based AI offers an antidote to LLM hallucinations in RAG systems, with explainable inferences rooted in concrete facts. Yet, many in the industry still lack the knowledge and understanding to fully capture the power of reasoning.
Join this Ultimate Guide to Semantic Reasoning to learn the best practices of rule writing and how to use it to supercharge applications. Use the W3C standard, OWL, for ontological reasoning, and the widely used Datalog for more advanced functionality such as aggregation, negation, and filtering to build a working solution live in the workshop.
Discover how this enriched data, coupled with the advanced automation feature of incremental reasoning, is enabling real-world applications, including how to enhance RAG and LLM-based solutions.
For beginners and experts alike, no prior knowledge is required.
Key Topics
Semantic Reasoning & Knowledge-Based AIKnowledge GraphsQuerying Graph DatabasesWriting RulesWriting Ontologies
Target Audience
Knowledge EngineersData ScientistsData EngineersData AnalystsManagers of the above
We have run similar tutorials before with between 10 to 100 attendees each time. They have been praised widely by past attendees. These tutorials scale well and are appropriate regardless of the group size.
They are aimed at a spectrum of users, from the non-technical to technically minded but unfamiliar. We cover the basics so that everyone has the tools to follow along with the rest of the tutorial but move quickly onto the more advanced sections. Experts in the field will not find this useful.
Goals
Get hands-on experience using Semantic Reasoning and Knowledge Graphs in order to understand the extent to which it can be used to empower real-world use cases.
Session outline:
In this workshop, attendees will learn what reasoning is, what it can to do transform data, and crucially, how to do that themselves and how it supports real-world applications.
After a brief theoretical introduction to the subject, attendees will be expected to get hands-on with a reasoning engine in order to learn how to setup a reasoning-ready datastore, and how to reason over it using OWL and Datalog rules.
No prior experience is required as we will run through the process step-by-step, from start to finish.
Over the course of the tutorial attendees will learn:
•How to write and run a SPARQL query
•The importance of reasoning and its application
•How to write a Datalog rule
•How to apply and verify the rules they write
•The extended opportunities with reasoning
•How to create a solution that relies on reasoning
•How to achieve RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) with enriched data, KGs and LLMs
Format
This class is very hands-on. Each topic will first be demonstrated to the students so they can copy an ideal example and see the intended results in an informal teacher-student format. Then they will be given the opportunity to apply their new learned skills without immediate direction, writing rules and queries by themselves.
If at any point a participant requires some assistance, the lecturers will be on hand to help, whether that requires a minor hint, a refresh of the material, or gentle guidance.
Anyone of any skill level should leave this class knowing what reasoning is and how to implement it, so individual support is flexible depending on the needs of the group.

Title: All Data in one EKG, and one EKG for all Use Cases? A case for building a hybrid graph landscape
Speaker: Timm Amstein
Description:
The dream of the all-encompassing Enterprise Knowledge Graph, serving as the central semantic hub for the whole company has been seen as the holy grail of the Knowledge Graph world for a few years now. Due to a variety of reasons this dream rarely comes to fruition.
At the same time the number of systems in need of connected information is growing rapidly, especially due to the rise of Agentic AI. This is especially challenging since more of these do rely on rapid, near-real-time analysis and responses in contrast to more strategic analytics use cases.
As a solution architect designing graph-based applications this poses the question of what to suggest clients for the future. In my talk I will make an argument of how to utilize the power of graph in many different places throughout a modern enterprise landscape, while relying on a hybrid approach based on linked data principles.
So how many graphs do we actually need? Designed for intermediate technical audience with that has about bringing Graph into their ecosystem, I will take the audience on a journey to find out.
Attendees will leave with an understanding of a hybrid graph architecture, challenges of modern system design and a deeper understanding of existing limitations.

Title: Decoupling Schemas from Systems - A Unified Modeling Approach for Data Products and Semantic Interoperability
Speaker: Alaa Alweish & Cruce Saunders
Description:
Enterprise schemas are trapped inside their originating systems, creating a fundamental architectural problem that limits data product development and semantic interoperability. When customer data exists in CRM systems with embedded schemas, financial data in ERP systems with different modeling approaches, and operational data in various SaaS platforms, each schema becomes inseparable from its hosting system. This tight coupling forces every integration project to solve the same semantic mapping challenges independently.
Data Products (DPROD) promise to revolutionize how organizations package and share data assets, but current approaches still bind data product schemas to their source systems. Without decoupled, portable schema definitions, data products cannot achieve true semantic interoperability. Teams rebuild similar transformations, create incompatible data products, and lose semantic richness during cross-system integration.
The deeper issue is schema ownership fragmentation: customer concepts are "owned" by CRM systems, financial concepts by ERP systems, and operational concepts by various platforms. This system-centric thinking prevents the creation of unified business models that can span systems while preserving semantic relationships and business rules.
Connected Data London has championed knowledge graphs and semantic technology, but most implementations still struggle with schema portability across systems. Organizations invest in graph databases and semantic layers while still managing dozens of incompatible schema representations for the same business concepts.
The Data Product movement recognizes that data assets need formal contracts and governance, but without unified schema modeling, data products become another silo rather than interoperable building blocks. Each organization solves identical schema unification challenges in isolation: standardizing customer representations, harmonizing product catalogs, modeling temporal business relationships.
This represents a fundamental architectural shift opportunity: moving from system-centric schemas to business-centric unified models that can generate system-specific representations while maintaining semantic coherence across the enterprise ecosystem.
We developed an approach for schema decoupling and unification that separates business concept modeling from system-specific implementations. The methodology involves:
Unified Business Models: Define canonical representations of business concepts (Customer, Product, Transaction, Asset) independent of any source system, capturing relationships, constraints, and business rules that span multiple systems.
System Mapping Architecture: Create typed correspondences between unified models and each system's schema representation, preserving semantic relationships while handling format differences, naming variations, and structural incompatibilities.
Multi-Target Schema Generation: From unified models, generate system-specific schema artifacts including database views, API contracts, data product schemas, graph representations, and validation rules—ensuring semantic consistency across all representations.
Portable Data Product Contracts: Enable DPROD implementations where data products reference unified schemas rather than system-specific formats, creating true interoperability between data products from different domains and systems.
This approach has been implemented across domains including biomedical research (managing complex research data standards), financial services (risk and compliance modeling), and manufacturing (asset and process modeling), demonstrating that unified schema modeling works across diverse industries and use cases.
Organizations implementing this approach report significant improvements in data product interoperability and reduced integration overhead. Cross-system integration time drops dramatically when teams can reference unified business models rather than mapping between dozens of system-specific schemas.
Data Product development accelerates because schemas become portable assets that travel with data, enabling semantic validation and automated transformation generation. Teams build comprehensive libraries of unified models that serve as the foundation for multiple data products while maintaining consistency across domains.
The unified modeling approach enables semantic layer implementations that truly span systems rather than aggregating incompatible representations. Schema changes propagate consistently across all generated artifacts, reducing the brittleness typically associated with multi-system data architectures.
Target Audience
Business/Technical: Mixed audience including data architects designing cross-system integration, data product developers seeking semantic interoperability, platform engineers building semantic infrastructure, and domain experts who understand business concepts that span multiple systems.
Level: Intermediate—attendees should understand schema design challenges and multi-system integration complexity. Familiarity with Data Products (DPROD) concepts beneficial but not required.
Required Background: Experience with enterprise data integration challenges and interest in semantic modeling approaches that span system boundaries.
Attendees will understand how to decouple schema definitions from system implementations, creating unified business models that enable true semantic interoperability. They'll learn:
Architectural patterns for separating business concept modeling from system-specific schemas
Methods for creating typed correspondences between unified models and diverse system representations
Strategies for generating multiple target formats from single unified schema definitions
Approaches to DPROD implementation using portable, semantically-rich schema contracts
Techniques for building unified model libraries that accelerate data product development
The session includes live demonstration showing transformation of system-bound schemas into unified business models, generation of multiple target representations from single models, and creation of interoperable data product contracts that maintain semantic richness across system boundaries.
Community Access: Attendees will see how unified models can be shared and discovered through collaborative libraries, enabling organizations to build upon proven schema patterns while contributing their own domain expertise to advance industry-wide semantic interoperability standards.

Title: Knowledge at the Fingertips for Field Service Engineers: Showcasing a business-oriented combination of knowledge graphs and large language models
Speaker: Prerna Juhlin
Description:
Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are experiencing a resurgence due to recent advancements in large language models (LLMs). This powerful combination is seen as highly beneficial for industries across various domains.
However, more than 70% of engineering leaders identify AI integration into applications and existing software engineering workflows as a major challenge, according to a Gartner 2025 survey. In addition to the technological advancements, relevant business aspects and integration of KGs and LLMs with existing business system landscapes must also be considered to drive business value.
Specifically in powertrain field service engineering, access to relevant knowledge for different drive, motor, and load assets are required to perform service and maintenance activities. Due to the typically siloed nature of different information sources, field service engineers need to rely on extensive manual efforts to connect the dots and identify the overall context, a time consuming and error-prone task.
Data integration remains a significant challenge across many industries. While combining the technologies of knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs) are expected to address this challenge, leveraging the technologies requires relevant business aspects into account into the development. This presentation will outline such an approach and showcase a novel application to field service engineering.
This presentation will outline a solution approach that integrates business and technology aspects as involved in the creation of a knowledge integration framework developed for ABB’s powertrain field service engineering to enhance business value.
Starting with business objectives, the solution first captures subject matter expert knowledge in an ontology that is subsequently aligned with relevant database schemas. Next, a knowledge graph is semi-automatically generated by combining data from relevant sources using a customization of the well-known Microsoft GraphRAG framework.
Using an RDF standards-based approach, deployment to different graph databases is enabled for increased flexibility. A system architecture integrates these novel developments with the current system landscape. Field service engineers can benefit from integrated and contextualized information based on this integration, resulting in having required knowledge at their fingertips for optimal performance.
The developed knowledge integration framework takes various aspects into account: business domain considerations, existing system landscape, selective use of large language models to enhance efficiency and semi-automated quality evaluations.
The development phase involved building proof-of-concepts for business stakeholders, agile practices with use-case oriented scaling of the ontology and knowledge graph, related knowledge transfers to development teams, which have all contributed to facilitating solution adoption.
The business-oriented development of the knowledge integration framework is expected to yield several benefits: improved time to fault resolution and customer satisfaction in powertrain service engineering; increased awareness of the value of connecting data for enhanced business value; improved alignment among business experts; as well as semantic interoperability across siloed databases.
Target audience:
Business and technicalIntermediateRequired backgroundBasic familiarity with knowledge graphs and large language models (LLMs)Awareness of common data integration challenges in industriesWhat will the people who attend your talk get from itEffective incorporation of business considerations into knowledge graph and LLM framework, illustrated via an example application for field service engineering.

Title: GraphRAG for Exploring Heterogeneous Medical Knowledge
Speaker: Giuseppe Futia
Description:
The growing complexity of healthcare data demands new approaches for knowledge integration and retrieval. In this masterclass, we present a methodology for building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) system that can leverage heterogeneous resources through a combination of materialized knowledge graphs and virtually integrated data sources.
The knowledge graph unifies information from medical ontologies, clinical documents, and reports. At the same time, electronic health records (EHRs) remain virtually connected—ensuring that sensitive data is not replicated, yet can still enrich reasoning. This hybrid design separates structural knowledge from patient-level data, allowing for flexible integration and deployment that is compliant with regulations.
We will demonstrate how the GraphRAG system leverages this ecosystem by dynamically orchestrating queries across ontologies, documents, and EHRs, reconciling heterogeneous information, and generating answers that are traceable, explainable, and historically contextualized.
Unlike traditional RAG, which primarily augments generation with unstructured text, our approach integrates temporal and semantic dimensions via the graph, supporting richer historical analyses and more robust explanations.
Participants will gain both conceptual and practical insights into designing graph-powered RAG systems for domains where trust, interpretability, and integration of diverse knowledge are essential.

Title: Crafting RDF - Generating Knowledge Graphs from Legacy Data
Speaker: Ora Lassila
Description:
A key part of any knowledge graph -based system is the ETL pipeline that produces graph data from legacy data sources. The so-called “Semantic Web stack” contains several standardized and mature technologies to implement these pipelines.
In this presentation we cover how to “craft RDF” using existing standards and their open-source implementations.
Specifically, we will cover R2RML and RML (for mapping tabular data to RDF), XSLT (for translating legacy XML to RDF), JSON-LD (for translating “plain vanilla” JSON to RDF), SHACL (for verifying and validating the outcome), and harvesting RDF from file systems and Web sites.
Building knowledge graphs using RDF and the rest of the "Semantic Web stack" is not "rocket science". The requisite tools and standards exist and are mature. What is needed is a collection of examples, recipies, and best practices that help developers get started.
The target audience for this presentation: technical, beginner/intermediate, with some background in RDF and related technologies. People who attend this talk will take home a sense of empowerment to tackle their data transformation and knowledge graph construction challenges.

Title: Beyond Technology: The Human blueprint for building an Enterprise Knowledge Graph
Speaker: Tara Raafat
Description:
Building a knowledge graph (KG) in an enterprise is more than a technical project. It is a human and organizational journey. At its core, it requires collaboration across teams, alignment of business priorities, and the creation of a shared language for data and knowledge. Enterprises that embark on this journey face a series of people-centered decisions. Where should the process begin in order to build trust and momentum? Should you cultivate in-house expertise or rely on external partnerships? How do you assemble a multidisciplinary team that blends business insight with technical skill? What practices encourage adoption, alignment, and enthusiasm across stakeholders, especially at the leadership level? What team structure builds the right balance between subject matter expertise, ontological rigor, and product delivery?
In this talk, I will share lessons from working with organizations of different sizes and industries, from small firms to global corporations. Together, we will explore the critical conversations and decisions that shape a successful knowledge graph initiative. We will discuss how to secure executive sponsorship, manage expectations, and bring diverse stakeholders into alignment. We will also look at timelines for building confidence, selecting the right early use cases, and demonstrating tangible value. This will be framed in the context of the unique cultural and organizational challenges that every enterprise faces depending on its size, business type, and stage of both technological and knowledge maturity.
Target audience : Knowledge engineers, strategists, AI experts or anyone interested in introducing Knowledge graphs in their organization.
Objectives : Whether you are just beginning your knowledge graph journey or seeking to optimize an ongoing implementation, this talk will equip you with actionable frameworks and strategies to succeed in building an enterprise-grade knowledge graph By helping you understand the intersection of strategic vision, technical excellence, people and organizational alignment.

Title: Demystifying Knowledge Graphs, Semantic Technologies and Labelled Property Graphs: A Beginners Hands-On Exploration for making the right choice
Speaker: Tara Raafat & Petra Selmer
Description:
Knowledge graphs have long underpinned enterprise data strategies, implemented through diverse paradigms ranging from RDF-based semantic technologies to labelled property graphs (LPGs). While these frameworks have often operated quietly in the background, the rise of large language models (LLMs) has reignited interest in knowledge graphs, bringing long-overdue recognition to their strategic value. Knowledge graphs not only enhance LLM training and deployment but also offer unmatched capabilities for optimizing data integration, governance, and analytics.
Yet, fundamental questions remain: What exactly constitutes a knowledge graph? When should RDF, OWL, or LPGs be applied? Are these technologies interchangeable, complementary, or competitive?
This tutorial seeks to demystify these approaches through a pragmatic, hands-on lens. Presenters—bringing distinct perspectives from both RDF and LPG traditions—will guide participants through real-world scenarios, comparative exercises, and applied case studies. Attendees will gain a nuanced understanding of the trade-offs, synergies, and integration pathways across semantic technologies, property graphs, and their integration with LLMs, equipping them to make informed architectural choices in enterprise and research settings.
Participants will explore:
The core principles and unique capabilities of semantic technologies and property graphs.Practical decision-making frameworks for selecting the right approach for specific use cases.Insights into emerging trends where these approaches converge to unlock new opportunities.Considerations to take into account when choosing the tools in order to ensure a smooth implementation.
Learn about some high level strategies for leveraging graph technologies to augment LLMs and drive business value.
By the end of the session, attendees will have a deeper understanding of the strengths, limitations and synergies of these graph based approaches, enabling them to make informed decisions that align with their organizational goals when solving different challenges.
Target Audience
Whether you're a technical leader, data scientist, engineer or enterprise strategist, this tutorial will equip you with actionable insights to harness the full potential of graphs in relevance to your use case.

Title: Model Once, Represent Everywhere: UDA (Unified Data Architecture) at Netflix
Speaker: Alexandre Bertails
Description:
As Netflix has expanded, core business concepts like “movie” or “actor” are modeled differently across teams and systems. Our current information architecture reflects this fragmentation: each domain operates with only a partial view of the business, building its own model of the world shaped by local needs and limited by system boundaries.
UDA (Unified Data Architecture) is the foundation for connected data in Content Engineering at Netflix. It enables teams to model domains once and represent them consistently across systems, powering automation, discoverability, and semantic interoperability.
In this talk, I will discuss how UDA operationalizes RDF: from domain modeling with its Upper metamodel, to semantic-preserving projections like GraphQL and Avro, and finally to automated data movement within a unified knowledge graph

Title: Text, Images, and Audio for Multimodal Intelligence in GraphRAG
Speaker: Amy Hodler & David Hughes
Description:
Vector searches alone no longer suffice, and integrating graphs with RAG processes has demonstrated clear benefits in enhancing the accuracy and explainability of GenAI. By enhancing vector searches with global enrichment and domain-specific grounding, graphs provide a powerful framework for tackling messy data by creating richer, more complete representations that overcome ambiguity inherent in single modalities.
So it’s no surprise that the GraphRAG bandwagon is getting pretty crowded these days—from academic papers to GitHub repos that multiply like rabbits, everyone is jumping on board. However, as anyone who’s worked with graphs knows, they require careful iteration and refinement to deliver the best results.
While the current GraphRAG crowd is obsessing over text and lexical graphs, they're missing the elephant in the room—all that juicy non-text data just sitting there untapped. Images and audio are rich with latent signals that are often ignored, despite their ability to add significant context to AI workflows. The next big leap for GraphRAG lies in fully integrating these multimodal data sources, creating a more comprehensive and explainable approach.
In this two-hour masterclass, we’ll introduce Multimodal GraphRAG (mmGraphRAG)—a cutting-edge framework that combines the semantic richness of images, audio, and text with the contextual reasoning power of graphs. This transformative approach enables an associative intelligence that moves search and analytics closer to the way humans abstract concepts and connect ideas.
We’ll guide you through the high-level architecture of mmGraphRAG and explore how associative intelligence drives its capabilities. You’ll see how agentic workflows can transform unstructured text into clean, validated graph data using tools like Boundary BAML for consistent data extraction and validation - as well as agent orchestration.
And you’ll lean how to combine graph and vector data for optimal associations using open source graph and vector databases. Join us to explore how integrating multimodal data into GraphRAG can transform the way we approach search, analytics, and AI-driven insights.
Key Topics
Expanding GraphRAG with Multimodal Data: How to incorporate images and audio into GraphRAG workflows to enhance understanding and context. Designing Multimodal Graph Schemas: Tips for customizing graph schemas and enabling multimodal searches that integrate visual and auditory elements. Hands-On Techniques: Practical guidance on creating embeddings from images and audio using interactive notebooks designed for experimentation. Future Applications: Insights into extending graph pattern analytics to different types of data for deeper contextual analysis.
Target Audience
Data and Knowledge Engineers Data Scientists and Machine Learning EngineersGoals
The goal of this masterclass is to give you a practical approach to move beyond text-only GraphRAG. We'll dive into how to integrate images and audio into your graph-based RAG pipelines, showing you how to design effective multimodal schemas and create embeddings from diverse data sources. By the end, you'll understand how Multimodal GraphRAG (mmGraphRAG) can deliver more accurate, explainable, and contextually rich AI solutions, bringing your search and analytics closer to how humans actually connect ideas.
Session outline:
Limitations of current GraphRAG approaches ○ Why vector search + lexical graphs fall short. ○ The potential of adding images, audio, and more. Dive into Multimodal GraphRAG (mmGraphRAG) Concepts of combining semantic richness with contextual reasoning. The implications of achieving associative intelligence and how it works. Building mmGraphRAG Strategies for incorporating images and audio into GraphRAG. Hands-on: Creating embeddings for images and audio (interactive notebook). Hands-on: Integrating intermediate results and query chaining Designing effective multimodal schemas. Future Applications Extending graph pattern analytics. Injecting temporal analysis in audio and images/videoFormat
This class is a mix of tutorials and hands-on opportunities. The beginning of the class will explore the high-level architecture before diving into practical design implications. From here we will work through the steps for decomposing images and audio into components that are loaded into a graph model. With this foundation in place, we will demonstrate how agents can utilize associative search to find semantic information and enrich them with insights from connected data, graphs, to surface key multimodal insights. You’ll have the chance to follow along in a Notebook that walks through how to blend graphs and embeddings in an embedding space to visualize associative search.
Level
Intermediate - Advanced

Comfortable with Python, Ollama, and basic graph and vector database concepts.

Title: How Wiz Became the Most Valuable Security Startup with Amazon Neptune
Speaker: Ian Robinson & Roy Reznik
Description:
In an era where cloud infrastructure spans millions of interconnected resources and security threats exploit the subtle relationships between them, traditional security approaches fall short.
Join  Roy Reznik, Co-Founder & VP R&D at Wiz, and Ian Robinson, AWS Specialist Solutions Architect for Data and Analytics, as they reveal how two industry leaders collaborated to build the world's largest cybersecurity graph—a breakthrough that's transforming how organizations understand and defend their cloud environments.
Wiz, the cybersecurity phenomenon recently acquired by Google for $32 billion, has redefined cloud security by providing comprehensive visibility across multi-cloud environments.
When Wiz set out to map the intricate web of relationships between cloud resources, identities, vulnerabilities, and threats across their customers' infrastructures, they needed a database that could handle unprecedented scale and complexity. The answer was Amazon Neptune, AWS's fully managed graph database service designed specifically for highly connected data.
This keynote takes you behind the scenes of an extraordinary technical collaboration. Ami Luttwak, who previously led Microsoft's Cloud Security Group and shaped products like Azure Security Center and Azure Sentinel, brings his 15+ years of cybersecurity expertise to explain why relationships matter in security.
Every cloud resource—from compute instances to storage buckets, from IAM roles to network configurations—exists in a complex web of connections. Understanding these relationships is the difference between catching a breach and missing it entirely.
Ian Robinson, coauthor of the seminal "Graph Databases" and a recognized expert in extracting value from connected data, demonstrates how Amazon Neptune's support for property graphs and Gremlin queries enabled Wiz to traverse billions of relationships in milliseconds.
Neptune's high performance, scalability, and durability proved essential for processing the massive, constantly evolving security graph that spans customers' entire cloud footprints.
Together, they'll showcase how this partnership created a graph containing billions of nodes and edges, representing cloud resources, their configurations, potential attack paths, and security risks across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
You'll learn how graph traversal queries identify critical vulnerabilities that traditional security tools miss—like discovering how an exposed S3 bucket connects through a chain of IAM roles to your production database, or how a misconfigured Kubernetes cluster creates an unexpected path to sensitive data.
The presentation reveals practical insights from building and operating this massive graph at scale: the architecture decisions, the query patterns that detect threats in real-time, and the lessons learned from pushing graph database technology to its limits.
Whether you're a security professional seeking to understand modern threat detection, a data architect designing systems for connected data, or a technologist interested in graph databases at scale, this keynote offers unprecedented insights into the intersection of cybersecurity and graph technology.
Discover how the world's biggest cybersecurity graph is helping organizations see their security posture not as isolated components, but as the interconnected system it truly is.

Title: The State of Graph in 2025: Categories, Use Cases, and Trends
Speaker: Timm Amstein & George Anadiotis & Alexandre Babeanu & Jean Villedieu
Description:
In the last couple of decades, Graph has gone from an emerging technology niche to an established market worth billions and rising with the AI tide.
With a multitude of offerings old and new, navigating this domain can be hard both for newcomers and seasoned users.
In this session, we offer a map to navigate the different categories of graph platforms and tools.
We examine what are the categories of offerings, and what each one is good at. We provide examples, share real-world use cases, and zoom in on emerging trends and future developments.
A focused 30-minute thought leadership panel examining the graph landscape in 2025. Designed for leaders who need actionable insights without deep technical detail.

Title: Scaling knowledge graphs and knowledge-based AI in the financial crime and KYC domain
Speaker: Lily Wang & Peter Crocker
Description:
Barclays has been exploring the use of semantic technology over the past few years. This talk shares our journey so far, exploring several use cases involving knowledge graphs and the use of reasoning via a semantic rules engine.
We’ll take a look at innovative AI applications that can scale expert knowledge within a regulated environment, where accuracy and performance are mission critical.
Whilst this talk aims to help CTOs and senior technical leaders sell the value of knowledge graphs and knowledge-based AI in their organization, we will also share some of the high-level concepts for the hands-on technical engineering audience.
We’ll focus on a use case related to financial crime and creating a unified view of entities (such as companies or people), to deliver improved operational efficiency, reduce compliance risk and improve customer experience. Other use cases will be explored including autonomous decisions and CRM.
We’ll cover an overview of knowledge-based AI, otherwise known as semantic reasoning, and how this is already being used in production and at scale to automatically enrich knowledge graphs with new facts based on expert knowledge.
We’ll see how an expressive rules language can be used to materialise new connections in the graph, including advanced concepts such as negation (finding the absence of data) and whole graph aggregation and calculations – both of which can transform knowledge graph value.
Finally, we will share practical tips on how attendees can get started with their own knowledge-based AI journeys.

Title: Beyond Chunking: SQL2Graph + Unstructured2Graph + MCP Client to Ship Explainable GraphRAG
Speaker: Marko Budiselic
Description:
Modern AI systems don’t fail on prompts - they fail on context.
Getting from raw enterprise data to explainable, multi-hop answers means (1) modeling well, (2) ingesting reliably and (3) interoperating across tools.
In this presentation, Marko Budiselic, CTO and cofounder of Memgraph, will show how teams can solve those three pain points with the Memgraph AI Toolkit:
SQL2Graph: Turn MySQL/Postgres schemas into validated property graphs. HyGM (Hypothetical Graph Model) proposes an initial model, explains trade-offs, accepts feedback, and validates before migration — taming junction tables, surrogate keys, and denormalization without hand-rolled ETL.Unstructured2Graph: Convert PDFs/DOCX/TXT into graph context with page-level provenance. LLM-assisted entity extraction links mentions to sources, enabling hybrid retrieval (vector + attributes + topology) and traceable answers.MCP Client in Memgraph Lab: Interoperate with the broader Model Context Protocol ecosystem. Connect Memgraph’s MCP Server and other MCP Servers to fetch, fuse, and orchestrate context across systems.It is all about solving pain points engineers have and Marko will address the following ones:
Schema-to-graph modeling uncertainty, cardinality explosions, and reworkUnstructured-data extraction/disambiguation with preserved provenanceGlue-code fatigue across tools; lack of standardization for agent workflowsLatency, explainability, and update cycles for continuously changing dataBy the end of the presentation, you should leave with a repeatable path from SQL to a validated model to Memgraph and an E2E pipeline from Docs to entities/relations to queryable graph with provenance.

Title: Innovation in Graph Databases and High-Performance Graph Engines: Adoption, Trends, and Getting Started
Speaker: Amy Hodler & Bradley Rees & David Hughes & Remy Boutonnet
Description:
Graph databases have evolved from niche technology to essential infrastructure for modern data-driven applications. With the rise of AI, real-time analytics, and complex relationship modeling, high-performance graph engines are becoming critical for competitive advantage.
This panel explores the current state of graph database adoption, breakthrough innovations, practical implementation strategies, and emerging trends shaping the future.

Title: Breaking Supply Chain Reactions: Graphs vs. Tariffs & Risks
Speaker: Maya Natarajan
Description:
The 2025 U.S. tariffs have sent shockwaves through global supply chains, exposing the limits of traditional data systems in managing increasingly complex risks and dependencies. Only graph technology can comprehensively address these challenges by transforming supply chains into dynamic, interconnected networks, enabling real-time visualization, analysis, and proactive risk management—capabilities that conventional systems cannot match.
In this session, we will begin with the foundational structures that underpin graphs and explore how graphs naturally model complex relationships—capturing small and wide data, interdependencies, hierarchies, legacy links, and hidden connections—that together form the critical fingerprints of risk. We then reframe supply chains as living graphs, where disruptions such as tariffs, extreme weather, and component shortages cascade like domino effects through a tightly woven network.
Through case studies, we will demonstrate resilience enabled by graph analytics:
Scoutbee: Cut supplier discovery time by 75% during extreme weather disruptions.Transparency-One: Provides full traceability for faster shortage response and compliance.U.S. Army: Unified Bill of Materials data for 8x faster strategic readiness analysis.Bridging business strategy and technical insight, this session reveals how graph algorithms transform tariff-related challenges into solvable problems—such as identifying alternative sourcing via betweenness centrality, modeling product redesign impacts, and clustering supplier risks. Attendees will learn why mastering graph is key to building resilient, agile supply chains capable of thriving through trade turbulence.
Who Should Attend:
Technical professionals, business analysts, and decision-makers with basic to intermediate AI and data analysis skills who want to use graph to solve complex supply chain challenges.
By attending, you will learn how to:
Use graph-based risk archetypes to anticipate and mitigate cascading supply chain disruptions.Apply techniques to map and simulate multi-tier supplier networks for early vulnerability detection.Implement proven strategies to accelerate decision-making and enhance supply chain resilience amid volatility.

Title: Knowledge Graphs in 2025 - from zero to mastery: Adoption, Implementation & AI Integration
Speaker: Priyanka Dank & Larry Swanson & John Placek & Ravinder Singh
Description:
In this panel, we'll discuss the growing adoption of semantic technology in business. We'll share success stories that illustrate the benefits of knowledge graphs, show examples of how this foundational technology fits into the broader AI ecosystem, and set out practical implementation pathways to help you get started on your journey to a fully intelligent AI architecture.

Current state of knowledge graph adoption across industriesPractical implementation framework and getting started strategiesKnowledge graphs and Generative AI integrationCommon roadblocks and proven solutionsROI measurement and business value demonstration
