Title: Vodafone's Journey: Semantic models in action
Speaker: Torsten Jedicke & Robin Osagie
Description:
From digital transformation to zero-touch automation, Vodafone’s ambition to drive more automation into network processes kept running into a recurring stumbling block, data. There was plenty of it, but fragmented across systems, trapped in silos and with varying levels of quality. As a result, automation workflows were slowed or derailed and the vision of zero-touch remained out of reach.
In this talk, we explore Vodafone’s journey, how the organisation evolved from traditional integration approaches to semantic modeling and how semantics is now closing the gaps of fragmentation, addressing data quality and providing the foundation for not only automation, but true autonomy.
This is not theory, but a lived story of how semantics and modeling are bringing clarity to one of the world’s most complex networks

Title: GraphRAG to RDF: Semantic Evolution of LPG Knowledge Graphs
Speaker: Kevin Phillips & Charles Ivie
Description:
Explore the seamless transformation of lexical property graphs into semantic RDF knowledge graphs using the GraphRAG Toolkit.
This session demonstrates how to get the best of both worlds: combining GraphRAG's powerful LPG-based RAG capabilities with the semantic richness of RDF.
Learn practical techniques for mapping lexical structures to established ontologies and taxonomies, ensuring consistency and interoperability.
Discover how this conversion process enhances your graph's semantic expressiveness while maintaining the original context and relationships, enabling more powerful querying and inference capabilities across your knowledge architecture.

Title: Ontology is not a trademark of RDF: LEX schemas for property graphs
Speaker: Alastair Green
Description:
Schemas for graphs are useful. From RAG to natural language text-to-graph queries, and for all the usual data modelling and database efficiency reasons, graphs need schemas just as much as collections of tables do.
The lack of a sophisticated schema standard for property graphs has led to the widely-spread idea that "Ontologies and vocabularies are the property of the RDF world, which is where knowledge graphs therefore belong". But of course, this is an accident of history.
The LEX project extends GQL property graph types to give schema capabilities comparable to those available in SQL and in RDF Schema + SHACL Core Constraints/JSON Schema. This talk explains how LEX works, using the Grasch LEX library, which has been produced in Python using Kiro's specification-led-development AI.
This Grasch library is an open-source project from the Graph Data Council (which incorporates Linked Data Benchmark Council). It is designed to be used (and expanded) to co-exist with multiple, pluggable property graph systems, and to allow on- and off-line graph validation, as well as visualizations and serializations.
The Graph Data Council has a liaison with WG3, the ISO/IEC standards committee for SQL and GQL, and aspects of LEX are likely to migrate into the GQL standard over time. One example is the provision of a standard "Information Schema" graph, to allow the exploration of graph types as schema graphs.
This talk is of interest to business and technical leaders and practitioners who are interested in the use of property graph schema in applications, products, projects and curated data sets.
LEX fills a crucial gap in the GDC TEXT2GRAPH benchmark project, and anyone looking to exploit natural language interfaces will want to see how LEX schemas help solve the problem of NL graph querying.
Some familiarity with property graphs, RDF and SQL data modelling and schema standards will help attendees get the most out of this intermediate-level presentation, but the ideas behind schema are straightforward, and the idea of using schema graphs to dictate correct data graphs is intuitive.
The win here is turning that intuition into a practical reality, and framing it as a standard.

Title: Semantic Data Products and industrial / AI applications at Zeiss
Speaker: Norbert Gergely & Yuan Gao
Description:
In the current context of data management augmentation through usage of GenAI, agentic and conversational techniques, the value of correctly defined and business driven semantic solutions is clearly increasing.
Given the new requirements in the area of digital manufacturing, digital twins and interpretation / diagnostics supported by optical / medical devices, the adaption of scalable, user-friendly data interoperability and composability applications at Zeiss is a must.
Technological innovations (linked / conversational search, agentic data / knowledge mapping, semantic conformation) and granular governance in form of semantic data products and domain centred ontologies are the current focus of this presentation.
How companies can benefit of such a direction, how one can create an end-2-end low-code / no-code application around it, which are the recommendations and possible pitfalls, what are the important measures to take, are all part of this semantically oriented journey.
